en: The Oranjeboomstraat is a street in the Rotterdam district of Feijenoord. While the rest of the Dutch people emphasize the second syllable when pronouncing the name (Oránjeboomstraat), the Rotterdammers do so only on the fourth, and they pronounce the name as Oranjebóómstraat.

name: Oranjebrug
en: The Oranjebrug is a bascule bridge in the city of Utrecht, spanning the Vaartsche Rijn. The bridge has a single passage opening for ships up to and including CEMT class II. It forms a relatively important link between the Hoograven neighborhood (eastern bank) and the Rivierenwijk (western bank), and is located between the Waalstraat and the Diamantweg.

name: Oranjehaven
en: Oranjehaven (also known as: Orange Haven) was a society in London during World War II.

name: Orgelpark
en: The Orgelpark is an arts centre in Amsterdam devoted to the organ, opened on 20 January 2007. It makes it possible to combine organ music with other art forms such as dance, ballet and theatre. There are several organs as well as other keyboard instruments.

name: Orgelpark
en: The Orgelpark is an art center in Amsterdam where the organ is central. It was opened on January 20, 2007. The Orgelpark provides the opportunity to combine organ music with other forms of art, such as dance, ballet and theater. There are several organs, but also other keyboard instruments present.

name: Osdorpergracht
en: The Osdorpergracht is a short canal in the Osdorp district in the city of Amsterdam. The canal was dug during the construction of the district and runs from the Sloterplas, near the apartment buildings of Torenwijck, along Osdorpplein and L. van Sonsbeeckstraat to the Hoekenesgracht at Tussen Meer.

name: Osdorperwegbrug
en: The Osdorperwegbrug, also known as Viaduct Rijksweg 5 – Osdorperweg and designated Kunstwerk 512 by Rijkswaterstaat, is a viaduct over the Osdorperweg in Amsterdam. It lies in the Westrandweg, the part of the A5 motorway that also crosses the Ringvaart of the Haarlemmermeer. It was designed by Zwarts & Jansma Architecten.

name: Osdorperwegbrug
en: The Osdorperwegbrug, also known as Viaduct Rijksweg 5 - Osdorperweg, designated by the Rijkswaterstaat operator as Work of Art 512, is a viaduct over the Osdorperweg in the municipality of Amsterdam. The building is located on the Westrandweg, a part of the A5 motorway that also runs over the Ringvaart of the Haarlemmermeer.

name: Oude Haagsebrug
en: The Oude Haagsebrug (bridge no. 1864) was a bridge over the Ringvaart of the Haarlemmermeer on the route between Amsterdam, via the hamlet of Nieuwe Meer, and Schiphol. The road over this bridge is the Oude Haagseweg, the former Rijksweg 4.

name: Oude Haagseweg
en: The Oude Haagseweg is a road in Sloten in the municipality of Amsterdam, formed by the remaining part of the first highway from Amsterdam to The Hague.

name: Oude Haagweg
en: The Oude Haagweg is a road in The Hague. This is part of an ancient connection that runs from Monster to The Hague. The connection is not entirely free (more) from fast traffic: the Loosduinse Hoofdplein is a pedestrian area and the Westeinde has one-way traffic. East of the Oude Haagweg, it transitions into the Loosduinseweg/-kade and then

name: Oude Hortus
en: The Oude Hortus refers to the garden, which from 1723 to 1920 was the botanical garden (hortus botanicus) of the University of Utrecht. The Oude Hortus is located between Lange Nieuwstraat and Nieuwegracht.

name: Oude Houthaven
en: The Houthavens are a group of harbors along the IJ in the Western Harbor Area of Amsterdam. On the north side, the harbors are bordered by the breakwater in the IJ, on the south side by the Spaarndammerbuurt. The harbors are mainly used by inland shipping. On the southern shores of the Houthavens were wood storage sites and companies in the wood industry

name: Oude Kerk
en: The Oude Kerk is located in Keizerstraat, once one of the busiest shopping streets of Scheveningen, in the Dutch municipality of The Hague. The church is the oldest monument of the former fishing village. The Oude Kerk is a church of the Protestant church in Scheveningen and houses its Neighborhood Church Oude Kerk and the Reformed Church Thabor Sc.

name: Oude Kerk Charlois
en: The Oude Kerk is a church in the Rotterdam district of Charlois. The building is relatively new, but stands on the site of a much older church. The current church hall dates from 1868. The tower was ready as early as 1660. The Reformed Neighborhood Church Charlois of the Protestant Kerk in the Netherlands uses the church building.

name: Oude Kinkerbrug
en: The Oude Kinkerbrug (bridge 169) is a fixed bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum. It connects the Elandsgracht with the Kinkerstraat, spanning the Singelgracht between them. The Appeltjesmarkt lies to its north-east and Amsterdam's police headquarters of 1941 to its south-east. The Europarking car park is also nearby.

name: Oude Lutherse Kerk
en: The Oude Lutherse Kerk at Singel 411, corner Spui, in Amsterdam is a Lutheran church, built on the site where the Lutheran congregation hall used to stand. The church was built between 1632 and 1633 under the direction of Wessel Becker and Willem van Daelen.

name: Oude Waalsdorperweg
en: The Waalsdorperweg is a quiet residential street in the Benoordenhout in The Hague, but was for many years from around 1975 to 2008 a busy main road to Wassenaar. As early as 1559, the Waelstorperlaen was named, it is probably named after an even older place called Walinxdorp.

name: Oudemanhuispoort
en: Oudemanhuispoort, often abbreviated to OMHP, is a complex of buildings in Amsterdam between the Spui and the Waterlooplein. It is one of the main sites of the University of Amsterdam and houses the faculty of humanities. Built in the 17th century around a courtyard, it was originally a hospice for old men and women, and is a protected monument.

name: Oudemanhuispoort
en: Oudemanhuispoort (often abbreviated as: OMHP) is a complex of buildings in Amsterdam, between the Spui and the Waterlooplein. It is one of the main locations of the University of Amsterdam, the faculty of humanities is located there. It was built in the 17th century in a square shape and was originally used as an Old Men and Women's Hospital, it is b

name: Oudezijds Kolk
en: The Oudezijds Kolk is a narrow canal in the city center of Amsterdam. It runs via the Zeedijk to the Open Havenfront from the extension of the Oudezijds Achterburgwal. Like the Geldersekade, it borders the Prins Hendrikkade to the north. Via the Kolksluis, built at the beginning of the 15th century, it served as a drainage canal(s) when the IJ, now the Op

name: Oudkerkhof
en: The Oudkerkhof is a street in the Dutch city of Utrecht, running from the Stadhuisbrug in the west to the Domstraat in the east. A side street is the Korte Minrebroederstraat on the north side. The Oudkerkhof is located in the city center near one of the oldest places in the city. Between 690 and 780 AD, there was a cemetery here next to the castle Trecht.

name: Our Lady of Good Counsel Church
en: The Onze-Lieve-Vrouw-van-Goede-Raadkerk, or simply the Goede-Raadkerk, is a Roman Catholic church building on Bezuidenhoutseweg in the Hague district of Bezuidenhout. The church is dedicated to Our Lady of Good Counsel. Today, the church is used by the English-speaking Catholic parish Church or Our Savior.

name: Overschiebrug-Noord
en: The Overschiebrug-Noord (bridge 655) and Overschiebrug-Zuid (bridge 665) are two works of art in Amsterdam Nieuw-West. The two viaducts span the Overschiestraat. They provide the connection between the Henk Sneevlietweg and the Rijksweg 10/Ringweg-West.

name: Overschiebrug-Zuid
en: The Overschiebrug-Noord (bridge 655) and Overschiebrug-Zuid (bridge 665) are two works of art in Amsterdam Nieuw-West. The two viaducts span the Overschiestraat. They provide the connection between the Henk Sneevlietweg and the Rijksweg 10/Ringweg-West.

name: Overschiebrug-Zuid
en: The Overschiebrug-Noord (bridge 655) and Overschiebrug-Zuid (bridge 665) are two structures in Amsterdam Nieuw-West. The two viaducts span the Overschiestraat and link the Henk Sneevlietweg with Rijksweg 10, the western ring road. The northern bridge serves as the westbound exit and the southern one as the on-ramp from the west.

name: Overtoom
en: The Overtoom is a street in the West district of Amsterdam, between the Stadhouderskade and the Amstelveenseweg. The current Overtoom was called the Heiligeweg from 1345, because it led to the Miracle of Amsterdam. Along the Heiligeweg ran the Heiligewegsevaart, later called the Overtoomsevaart. A section of Overtoom was called Vondelkade for a short time.

name: P.W. Janssen
en: The Monument Peter Wilhelm Janssen is a memorial on the Bellamyplein in Amsterdam-West. The sculpture by Bart van Hove was unveiled on 29 May 1908 by Jacob Theodoor Cremer, former minister of colonies and chairman of the committee, who wanted a memorial to Peter Wilhelm Janssen, entrepreneur, philanthropist and co-founder of the Deli Maatschappij.

name: P.W. Janssen
en: The Monument Peter Wilhelm Janssen is a monument on Bellamyplein in Amsterdam-West. The image made by Bart van Hove was unveiled on May 29, 1908 by Jacob Theodoor Cremer, former minister of colonies and also chairman of the committee, who wanted to commemorate Peter Wilhelm Janssen, entrepreneur, philanthropist and co-founder of the Deli Maatsch

name: Paardenkathedraal
en: The Paardenkathedraal is a theater on Veeartsenijstraat in the Wittevrouwen district in the Dutch city of Utrecht. The building is a former riding school of the Rijks Veeartsenijschool, the later Faculty of Veterinary Medicine of the University of Utrecht.

name: Paddepoel
en: Paddepoel is an area north of the city of Groningen, located globally between the Reitdiep and the Paddepoelsterweg, with Wierumerschouw as the northernmost point. This area also contains the Paddepoel urban district. Paddepoel is located in the municipality of Groningen as well as the municipality of Het Hogeland.

name: Paleis Lofen
en: Lofen was a palace of the German emperors that was built around 1020 in Utrecht on the Trecht castle. This palace was located between the current Domplein and the Oudegracht and bordered the immunity of the ecclesiastical area within the castle. In a charter from 1122, Lofen is mentioned in Latin as: palacio imperatoris in Traiecto, quod vulgo Lofen dicitur,

name: Paleis voor Volksvlijtbrug
en: The Paleis voor Volksvlijtbrug (bridge no. 248) is a fixed bridge on the boundary of Amsterdam-Centrum and Amsterdam Oud-Zuid. It connects the Westeinde on the north side with the Stadhouderskade, the south quay of the Singelgracht, and the Van Woustraat, spanning the Singelgracht. Tram line 4 runs over it.

name: Paleiskerk
en: The Paleiskerk or Baptist church in The Hague is a neo-Romanesque church from 1886 on Paleisstraat, near Paleis Noordeinde.

name: Pancratiuskerk
en: The Sint-Pancratiuskerk is a Roman Catholic church in the village of Sloten. The first Sloten church is first mentioned in a charter of Bishop Willem I of Gelre from 1063. It may have stood near the present Van Suchtelen van de Haarestraat in Osdorp, between the Osdorpplein and Hoekenes. The village has been on its present site since about 1175.

name: Pancratiuskerk
en: The Sint-Pancratiuskerk is a Roman Catholic church in the village of Sloten. The first Sloterkerk is first mentioned in a charter of Bishop Willem I (van Gelre) from 1063. This church may have stood near the current Van Suchtelen van de Haarestraat in Osdorp (between the Osdorpplein and Hoekenes). Since around 1175, the village has been

name: Paradijskerk
en: The Paradijskerk is an old Catholic church building on the Nieuwe Binnenweg in Rotterdam.

name: Park de Gagel
en: Park de Gagel is a park in the Overvecht district of the city of Utrecht. The name comes from the nearby Fort De Gagel. The park is surrounded by the Gangesdreef, Carnegiedreef, Gambiadreef When the Jaarbeurs was demolished at the Vredenburg in 1970, the rubble was dumped at this location, creating an artificial hill in the park. The ground of the

name: Park De Kuil
en: Park de Kuil is a park in Amsterdam Nieuw-West.

name: Park de Schinkeleilanden
en: The Park Schinkeleilanden is located in Amsterdam-Zuid west of the Olympic Stadium along the Schinkel. From the Olympic Quarter, the park can be reached via the Jan Wilsbrug. The railway line from Haarlemmermeer station in the direction of Amstelveen is located over two (almost) islands between the Schinkel and the Stadiongracht.

name: Park de Watertoren
en: Park de Watertoren is a large park in the Overvecht district in the Dutch city of Utrecht. The park was laid out around 1975, around the 1935 water tower. The park is crossed by the Marnedreef and the Moezeldreef.

name: Park Groot Zandveld
en: Park Groot Zandveld is a partly built city park in the Utrecht neighborhood/subdistrict Het Zand, which is part of the Leidsche Rijn district. The relatively small-scale area was developed at the beginning of the 21st century with the construction of the Vinex site Leidsche Rijn.

name: Park Nieuweroord
en: Park Nieuweroord is a park in the Dutch city of Utrecht. It is located on the west side of the Inner City. Previously, Nieuweroord consisted of a country house and a park on and around this location.

name: Park Somerlust
en: Park Somerlust is a park in Amsterdam-Oost

name: Park Transwijk
en: Park Transwijk is a city park in the Dutch city of Utrecht. The park was built between 1956 and 1964, at the same time as the construction of the southwestern districts of Transwijk and Kanaleneiland. A strict design was used in the layout. In 2001, the park was redesigned again. The park includes a children's farm, among other things.

name: Parkhaven
en: The Parkhaven is a harbor from the period of the turn of the century to the twentieth century, located between the Lloyd Quarter and the Park in Rotterdam. The Parkhaven was dug between 1890 and 1893 and was equipped between 1903 and 1908 for the transfer of bulk goods, as on the east side, where warehouses of Van Ommeren stood.

name: Parkweg
en: Parkweg can refer to: Parkweg (Maarssen), a street in the Dutch village of Maarssen Parkweg (metro station), a metro station in Schiedam of the Rotterdam metro Parkweg (Nijmegen), a street in the Dutch city of Nijmegen Parkweg (Voorburg), a street in the Dutch town of Voorburg

name: Parnassusweg
en: The Parnassusweg is a street in the Amsterdam district of Zuid. The street was named in 1929 after the Greek mountain Parnassus.

name: Pastoorsbrug
en: The Pastoorsbrug (bridge 55) is a fixed bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum. It lies in the southern quay of the Brouwersgracht and crosses the Keizersgracht, making it the northernmost bridge over that canal, which does not continue beyond the Brouwersgracht. Too young to be a monument itself, it is surrounded by national monuments.

name: Pastoorsbrug
en: The Pastoorsbrug (bridge 55) is a fixed bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum. The bridge is located on the southern quay of the Brouwersgracht and crosses the Keizersgracht. It is therefore the northernmost bridge over that canal that does not continue on the other side of the Brouwersgracht.

name: Pathé Buitenhof
en: Pathé Buitenhof is a cinema in The Hague at the Buitenhof of Pathé Nederland.

name: Pathé City
en: The Pathé City is a Pathé cinema at Kleine-Gartmanplantsoen 15-19 in Amsterdam, 40 meters from Leidseplein and diagonally opposite De Balie. The cinema is located in the City Theater building, a theater building from 1935. Initially, it was set up with a single large theater hall. The first film that was shown in the cinema was Episode by reg

name: Pathé de Kuip
en: Pathé de Kuip was opened in 2002 and is a megaplex operated by Pathé Netherlands. The cinema has 14 halls spread over 3 floors with a total of 2746 seats. With this capacity, this is the largest cinema in the Rotterdam region and one of the busiest cinemas in the Netherlands. The name of this cinema is derived from the adjacent football

name: Pathé de Munt
en: Pathé de Munt is a large cinema in the center of Amsterdam of cinema operator Pathé. The cinema is located on Vijzelstraat not far from another Pathé cinema: Pathé Tuschinski in Reguliersbreestraat. Both cinemas border each other behind the shops on Reguliersbreestraat. The cinema has 13 rooms, divided over three

name: Pathé Rembrandt Utrecht
en: Pathé Rembrandt Utrecht is a cinema on the Oudegracht in the Dutch city of Utrecht. The cinema is part of the Pathé cinema chain and has three halls (the smallest number of all Pathé cinemas in the Netherlands) with a total of 683 seats.

name: Pathé Utrecht Leidsche Rijn
en: Pathé Utrecht Leidsche Rijn is a Dutch cinema in Utrecht. The building is located on Berlinplein, on the roof of the Leidsche Rijntunnel on the A2. The cinema has seven halls (1574 seats), the largest of which can accommodate over 284 visitors. The theater also has a rooftop terrace with views of the city. Since 2017, in

name: Paulusbrug
en: The Paulusbrug is a national monument arched bridge in the center of the Dutch city of Utrecht. The bridge spans the Nieuwegracht and has a single span. On the bridge border are yards, a stone yard staircase and yard cellars. The Hamburgerstraat and Herenstraat run along the Paulusbrug. The Paulusbrug is one of the oldest bridges over this end-14th-century

name: Pauluskerk
en: The Willem de Zwijgerkerk or Sint-Pauluskerk is a Roman Catholic parish church on the Willem de Zwijgerplantsoen in the Dutch city of Utrecht. The church has a hexagonal shape and is built according to the central building. On the roof there is a bell tower.

name: Pauluskerk
en: The Willem de Zwijgerkerk or Sint-Pauluskerk is a Roman Catholic parish church on the Willem de Zwijgerplantsoen in the Dutch city of Utrecht. The church has a hexagonal shape and is built according to the central building. On the roof there is a bell tower.

name: Pauluskerk
en: Pauluskerk is a church building on Mauritsweg in the center of Rotterdam. The first Pauluskerk there was inaugurated in 1960 by the Reformed Church of Rotterdam (now part of the Protestant Church in the Netherlands) and was demolished in 2007. At the same location, church activities resumed in 2013 in a new futuristic-looking building.

name: Pelikaanbrug
en: The Pelikaanbrug (bridge number 277) is a lifting bridge from 1984 in Amsterdam-Centrum, near the Oosterkerk. The bridge spans the Nieuwe Vaart, from the Hoogte Kadijk in the south to the Wittenburgergracht in the north. The bridge is exclusively accessible to pedestrians and cyclists. The bridge is named after the pelican, but also after the nearby former

name: Pelikaanbrug
en: The Pelikaanbrug (bridge number 277) is a drawbridge from 1984 in Amsterdam-Centrum, near the Oosterkerk. It spans the Nieuwe Vaart from the Hoogte Kadijk in the south to the Wittenburgergracht in the north, and is open only to pedestrians and cyclists. It is named after the pelican, and also after a nearby former works of that name.

name: Persoonshaven
en: The Persoonshaven is a port on Feijenoord in Rotterdam, on the left bank of the Nieuwe Maas.

name: Petemayenbrug
en: The Petemayenbrug is a double pickup bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum. The name is said to be derived from petemoeien (stepmother), also an indication of old women. It connects Bokkinghangen with Zandhoek, both western docks of the Westerdok. Bokkinghangen is located on the former Bolwerk Blauwhoofd (Zeeheldenbuurt), Zandhoek on the Realeneiland. It spans

name: Peter Postbrug
en: The Peter Postbrug (bridge 2162) is a structure in Amsterdam Nieuw-West. The Laan van Spartaan district in which it lies was laid out in the 2000s. Sports fields once on the city's edge became surrounded by building as Amsterdam needed room for housing, and a new district with new drainage channels was created.

name: Peter Postbrug
en: The Peter Postbrug (bridge 2162) is a structural work of art in Amsterdam Nieuw-West. The district Laan van Spartaan, in which this bridge is located, was developed in the early 21st century. Sports fields, once located on the outskirts of the city, were increasingly built on and Amsterdam needed space for housing. A new district and new drainage came about

name: Petroleumhaven
en: The Petroleumhaven is a port in the Amsterdam port area.

name: Petruskerk
en: The Petruskerk is a Protestant church in the former village of Sloterdijk, now part of Amsterdam-West.

name: Philips Willembrug
en: The Philips Willembrug is a bridge in the Dutch city of Rotterdam, in the Hillegersberg district. The bridge has a free passage height of KP +2.82 m and the width is 9.44 m. The bridge crosses the Rotte at the height of the Hillegersberg-Zuid district. The bridge is named after Prince Philip Willem of Orange (1554-1618).

name: Pia Beckbrug
en: The Pia Beckbrug (bridge number 1868) is a permanent bridge in Amsterdam-Slotervaart in Amsterdam Nieuw-West. The bridge was built to open up a neighborhood, whose names are named after jazz musicians such as Louis Armstrong, Duke Ellington and Count Basie.

name: Pia Beckbrug
en: The Pia Beckbrug (bridge number 1868) is a fixed bridge in Slotervaart, Amsterdam Nieuw-West. It was built to open up a district whose streets are named after jazz musicians such as Louis Armstrong, Duke Ellington and Count Basie. It was built in the late 1980s and early 1990s and lies in the Louis Armstrongstraat.

name: Pianola Museum
en: The Pianola Museum in the Jordaan is a music museum in Amsterdam that offers an overview of the history and way of playing the pianola, a 'self-playing' musical instrument that was built between 1900 and around 1935. The museum's collection includes more than 100 instruments from that time. Regular concerts with kl take place in the museum

name: Piet Bakkerbrug
en: The Piet Bakkerbrug (bridge number 715) is a fixed bridge in Amsterdam Nieuw-West. The traffic bridge, which also carries bus line 63, lies in the Pieter Calandlaan and spans the Christoffel Plantijngracht. It has seven lanes: footway, cycle path and carriageway eastbound, a central island, then carriageway and cycle path westbound.

name: Piet Bakkerbrug
en: The Piet Bakkerbrug (bridge number 715) is a permanent bridge in Amsterdam Nieuw-West. The traffic bridge, over which bus line 63 also runs, is located in Pieter Calandlaan and spans the Christoffel Plantijngracht.

name: Piet Heinkade
en: The Piet Heinkade is a street in the Eastern Harbor Area of Amsterdam. The quay runs along the extension of the De Ruijterkade (along the north side of Central Station) in an easterly direction to Rietlandpark, where it transitions into the Panamalaan. The street is part of the ring road S100. The Piet Heinkade was named after vice admiral Piet Hein in 1919

name: Piet Keizerbrug
en: The Piet Keizerbrug (bridge 2234) is a structural work of art in Amsterdam-Oost. The bridge is a pedestrian and bicycle bridge; it forms the connection between the Esplanade de Meer square and the Stade de Colombes (street). It lies parallel to the Sjaak Swartbrug over a decorative water.

name: Piet Keizerbrug
en: The Piet Keizerbrug (bridge 2234) is a structure in Amsterdam-Oost. It is a foot and cycle bridge connecting the Esplanade de Meer square with the Stade de Colombes. It runs parallel to the Sjaak Swartbrug over an ornamental water in the Park de Meer neighbourhood in Watergraafsmeer, built here between 1998 and 2002.

name: Piet Meerburgbrug
en: The Piet Meerburgbrug (bridge 234) is a fixed bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum. The traffic bridge spans two parallel diving boards. These diving boards connect a ornamental pond in the Hortus Botanicus Amsterdam with the water of the Nieuwe Keizersgracht.

name: Piet Meerburgbrug
en: The Piet Meerburgbrug (bridge 234) is a fixed bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum. The traffic bridge crosses two parallel culverts, which connect an ornamental pond in the Hortus Botanicus Amsterdam with the water of the Nieuwe Keizersgracht. It links the Hortusplantsoen on the west side with the northern quay of the Nieuwe Keizersgracht.

name: Piet Wiedijkpark
en: The Piet Wiedijkpark is a park in the Amsterdam district of Osdorp, Amsterdam Nieuw-West.

name: Pieter Calandlaan
en: The Pieter Calandlaan is a street in Amsterdam Nieuw-West.

name: Pieter de Hoochbrug
en: The Pieter de Hoochbrug is a double bascule bridge from 1932 in the Delfshaven district in the Dutch municipality of Rotterdam. It is a bridge over the Coolhaven, which was dug in 1922, the connection between the Nieuwe Maas and the Delfshavense Schie. The bridge is located along the Pieter de Hoochweg. The bridge is named after the Rotterdam art painter Pi

name: Pieter Goemansbrug
en: The Pieter Goemansbrug is a fixed bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum. It is named after the lyricist Pieter Goemans and was previously known unofficially as the Bestedelingenbrug or Bestedelingensluis, after the nearby Bestedelingenhuis, a refuge for orphans and the poor, which was merged with the then Palace of Justice in 1950.

name: Pieter Goemansbrug
en: The Pieter Goemansbrug is a fixed bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum. It is named after writer Pieter Goemans and was previously officially known as Bestedelingenbrug and/or Bestedelingensluis after the once nearby Bestedelingenhuis (care for orphans and poverty spreaders or, in other words, settlements), which was merged in 1950 with the then-Palace of

name: Pistoolhaven
en: The Pistoolhaven is a port in Rotterdam's Europoort on the Beerkanaal. The main user is the Loodswezen, but among others the Rotterdam Port Authority also uses it. Heliport Maasvlakte was or is also located here, used by the Loodswezen.

name: Planciusspoorbrug
en: The Planciusspoorbrug is a railway viaduct in Amsterdam-Centrum in the Netherlands. The bridge spans the north-south running Planciusstraat, its direct namesake, both are named after Petrus Plancius. Until November 2017, the bridge was known as S6 and S7 (rail bridge 6 and 7).

name: Planciusspoorbrug
en: The Planciusspoorbrug is a railway viaduct in Amsterdam-Centrum. It spans the north-south Planciusstraat, from which it takes its name; both are named after Petrus Plancius. Until November 2017 the bridge was known as S6 and S7, when the city renamed all the railway bridges in Amsterdam.

name: Plantage Doklaan
en: The Plantage Doklaan is a street in the Plantagebuurt of Amsterdam. The street runs along the Entrepotdok, which was built in 1857, and is named after it. Originally, the street ran from Plantage Parklaan to Plantage Muidergracht and was crossed halfway by Plantage Kerklaan. Between Plantage Kerklaan and Plantage Muidergracht is the street

name: Plaquette Chet Baker
en: The Chet Baker plaque is an artistic work in Amsterdam-Centrum, a small tribute to the trumpeter Chet Baker. On the night of 12-13 May 1988 he fell from the window of Hotel Prins Hendrik at Prins Hendrikkade 52-58, probably under the influence, and was left almost unrecognisable by his fall onto a bollard.

name: Plaquette Chet Baker
en: The Plaquette Chet Baker is an artistic work of art in Amsterdam-Centrum. It is a small tribute to the trumpeter Chet Baker. He died on the night of May 12 to 13, 1988, presumably under the influence, falling out of the window of Hotel Prins Hendrik, located at Prins Hendrikkade 52-58. He was almost unrecognizable after falling on a canal boat in Amsterdam.

name: Plein Theater
en: The PleinTheater in Amsterdam-Oost is a stage for small-scale theatre, dance, contemporary classical music, youth theatre and neighbourhood activities.

name: Pleinweg
en: The Pleinweg is an important traffic artery on Rotterdam-Zuid in the district of Charlois. The road connects Maastunnelplein with Strevelsweg at Zuidplein. It is part of the tunnel traverse.

name: Plesmanlaan
en: The Plesmanlaan is a street in Amsterdam - Nieuw West. The street runs along the Heemstedestraat, from the viaduct (Heemstedespoorbrug) of the Ring Line. The road runs to the village of Sloten, where the Plesmanlaan crosses the Osdorperweg into the Langsom street that leads to the Sloterbrug to Badhoevedorp.

name: Plompetorenbrug
en: The Plompetorenbrug is a nationally protected arched bridge in the center of the Dutch city of Utrecht. It is also the name of a street at this location. The bridge spans the Plompetorengracht which flows out under the bridge into the Stadsbuitengracht. The bridge has a single span and south of it are unused construction basements.

name: Plompetorengracht
en: The Plompetorengracht is a short canal and street in the city center of Utrecht.

name: Pniëlkerk
en: The Pniëlkerk is a monumental church building in the Dutch city of Utrecht. The church named after the biblical place Pniniel, originally built for Reformed people, is located near Oog in Al. It was built in 1954-1955 according to the design of Piet Dingemans and Sjoerd Wouda. The building has a hexagonal layout. Along the facades there is a hallway

name: Poldervaart
en: The Poldervaart is a partially canalized waterway in the Netherlands, between the Schie south of the Kandelaar and the Nieuwe Maas between Schiedam and Vlaardingen.

name: Polderweg
en: The Polderweg is a street in Amsterdam-Oost. The Polderweg runs from Linnaeusstraat in a northeast direction. At the railway line between Amsterdam Muiderpoort and Amsterdam Science Park there is a bend and the street continues in a southeast direction to bridge 2360 over the Ringvaart.

name: Pompenburg
en: The Pompenburg is a street in the Dutch city of Rotterdam, between the Goudsesingel and the Hofplein. It is part of the city route S100 Centrumring. The street was named in 1949. Before World War II, this place was located on the Pompenburgsingel, which ran along the medieval city wall.

name: Poortershaven
en: Poortershaven is a small industrial area and a former port in the east of the Rotterdam municipality of Hoek van Holland. It is located on the Nieuwe Waterweg, just before the Schenkeldijk, against the municipal border with Maassluis.

name: Posthoornkerk
en: The Posthoornkerk, official name Our Lady of the Immaculate Conception, is a church building on Haarlemmerstraat in Amsterdam. The architect of the Posthoornkerk was P.J.H. Cuypers, who designed the building in 1860. The church replaced the dilapidated hiding church De Posthoorn on the Prinsengracht, whose name was taken over, after an earlier attempt by

name: Postjesbrug
en: Brug 231 may refer to Brug 231 (Houtgracht), a bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum over the Houtgracht, which was filled in in 1882, or Brug 231 (Postjeswetering), a bridge in Amsterdam-West from 1919/1920.

name: Postjeswetering
en: The Postjeswetering in Amsterdam-West was built in its current form in the 1920s as part of Plan West. The canal has been in the De Baarsjes district since 1990.

name: Praterlaan
en: The Gerrie Mührenbrug (bridge 2235) is a structure in Amsterdam-Oost. It is one of the traffic bridges — the others are for slow traffic — within the Park de Meer neighbourhood in the Watergraafsmeer, built here between 1998 and 2002. That neighbourhood is entirely surrounded by a ring ditch.

name: President Allendelaan
en: The President Allendelaan is an important main street in Amsterdam-West (S207) that connects the districts Slotermeer and Osdorp. The avenue runs from north to west, runs along the Slotermeerlaan and begins at the Sloterparkbad and the end point of tram line 7. Then the avenue continues with a bend further west and goes into Os

name: President Kennedylaan
en: The President Kennedylaan is a street in the Amsterdam Rivierenbuurt in the Zuid district.

name: Prins Bernhardplein
en: The Prins Bernhardplein is a square in the Amsterdam district of Watergraafsmeer. The square is located north of Amstel station and Julianaplein, south of Wibautstraat, west of Gooiseweg and east of Mr. Treublaan. The square was put into use on October 15, 1939 at the same time as the opening of Amstel station.

name: Prins Hendrikkade
en: The Kattenburgerplein is a square in Kattenburg in Amsterdam-Centrum. It lies along the Prins Hendrikkade, opposite Kadijksplein, across the Kattenburgerbrug over the Nieuwe Vaart. From the square, traffic can continue to the island of Kattenburg via Kattenburgerstraat, or via Kattenburgergracht to the other Eastern

name: Prins Maurits en de burgers van Den Haag
en: Prins Maurits en de burgers van Den Haag is a monument in honor of Prince Maurice located on the Heerenbrug in The Hague. The monument commemorates the fact that between 1613 and 1619 the citizens of The Hague, at the request of Maurice, dug a moat around the city that served as a defense of the city.

name: Prins Willem-Alexandersluis
en: The Oranjesluizen are a complex of sluice gates in the IJssel River. They form the border between the Inner and Outer IJssel and contribute to keeping the water level in the North Sea Canal at a constant level. They also ensure that too much salty water does not enter the IJsselmeer from the North Sea Canal.

name: Prinsengracht
en: The Prinsengracht is a canal in Amsterdam that runs parallel to the Keizersgracht. The canal, named after the Prince of Orange, is the fourth of the four main canals belonging to the Amsterdam canal belt.

name: Prinses Alexiahaven
en: The Prinses Alexiahaven is a Dutch port on the Rotterdam Second Maasvlakte. The port has a length of 7.62 km and is named after Princess Alexia of the Netherlands.

name: Prinses Amaliahaven
en: The Prinses Amaliahaven is a container port on the Rotterdam Second Maasvlakte. The port is located next to a 380 kV high-voltage substation and has a length of 5.76 km. The port is named after Princess Catharina-Amalia. On February 22, 2021, it was announced that the expansion of the port with 2.4 km of harbor quay walls was to be awarded.

name: Prinses Amaliaplein
en: The Prinses Amaliaplein is a square in Amsterdam-Zuid. The square can already be seen on Hendrik Petrus Berlage's Plan Zuid from 1917. It forms the final piece of the Minervalaan towards the Zuiderstation. However, it would take several years before the city reached this point, but the site plan has hardly changed. On that drawn plan is an open

name: Prinses Arianehaven
en: The Prinses Arianehaven is a port on the Rotterdam Second Maasvlakte. The port has a length of 4.76 km and is named after Princess Ariane of the Netherlands.

name: Prinses Irenebrug
en: The Prinses Irenebrug is a bridge in the Dutch city of Rotterdam, in the Hillegersberg district. The bridge has a height in closed position of KP +1.30 m, in raised position KP +2.90 m since its replacement in 2005, and the width is 5.70 m. The bridge crosses the Rotte and connects the Molenlaankwartier and Terbregge districts.

name: Prinses Irenestraat
en: The Prinses Irenestraat is a street in the Amsterdam district of Zuid, on the edge of the Zuidas. The street was named in 1953 and was named after Princess Irene, daughter of the then queen Juliana. The western part of the street changed its name after the renaming of Parnassusweg in 1977. This is now called Fred. Roeskestraat. With this, the

name: Prinses Julianakerk
en: The Prinses Julianakerk in The Hague is a church in the Scheveningen district of Duindorp. The church was built in a commercial-expressionist style and is located at the corner of Nieboerweg, Tesselsestraat and Vlielandsestraat. The architect W.Ch. Kuijpers also designed the Nieuwe Badkapel in Scheveningen.

name: Prinses Margriethaven
en: The Prinses Margriethaven is a port on the Rotterdam Second Maasvlakte and is named after Princess Margriet of the Netherlands. The port is located next to the APM Terminal and the Futureland visitor center.

name: Prinsessegracht
en: The bridges in The Hague were given names and numbers by the Hague Municipal Works, later incorporated into the Department of Urban Management, which were also applied to the bridges themselves through a GW number. Later these became DSB numbers.

name: Prinsestheater
en: The Prinses Theater is a theater in Delfshaven, Rotterdam. The American actress Jayne Mansfield promoted her film The Girl Can't Help It there in 1957, Lee Towers received the Wolfert van Borselenpenning there in 2000.

name: Professor Joop van Stigtpark
en: Professor Joop van Stigtpark is the unofficial name of a park-like environment in Amsterdam-Zuidoost. The park was named in 2013, when neighbors developed an initiative for naming a green strip with watercourse between the Gouden Leeuw and Groenhoven apartment blocks. This collection of apartments was built around 1974 according to the design of architect

name: Provincialeweg
en: Provincialeweg can refer to: Provincialeweg (Delft), see Prinses Beatrixlaan (Rijswijk/Delft) Provincialeweg (Schalkwijk)

name: Puntbrug
en: The Puntbrug is a swing bridge in the center of the Dutch city of Rotterdam. The bridge spans the Wijnhaven and connects the tip of the island between the Wijnhaven and the Scheepmakershaven to the north side of the Wijnhaven. The bridge is named after that point. In popular parlance, it is also known as the Kronkel (after its shape).

name: Puntegaalstraat
en: The Puntegaalstraat is a street in the Rotterdam district of Delfshaven. Among the inhabitants of the city, the street is better known as the Plukmekaalstraat; this after the office of the Tax and Customs Administration, which was located on this street from 1948 to 1996, where people felt "plucked bald".

name: Purmerplein
en: The Purmerplein in Amsterdam-North is a square in the village of Nieuwendam, which has belonged to the municipality of Amsterdam since 1921. The Purmerplein forms the center of Tuindorp Nieuwendam, an expansion district with mainly worker housing that was built between 1924 and 1934 under the direction of the Municipal Housing Service Amsterdam.

name: PVCV
en: PVCV (Patronaats Voetbalclub Vleuten) is an amateur football club from Vleuten in the Dutch municipality of Utrecht in the province of the same name.

name: Quintijnsbrug
en: The Quintijnsbrug is a nationally protected arched bridge in the center of the Dutch city of Utrecht. The bridge spans the Nieuwegracht, a canal that was built at the end of the 14th century. The stone bridge has a single span and one or more bridge cellars. On the bridge border a stone dockyard staircase, docks and dockyards.

name: Raampoort
en: Raampoort may refer to the Raampoort in Amsterdam, in Deventer, or in Haarlem.

name: Radio Museum
en: The Rotterdams Radio Museum Foundation was founded in 1988 by Harry de Jong sr., a former director of the Correct company. Volunteers work in the museum, located near NS Station Noord in the South Holland city of Rotterdam. The museum is open on Thursdays, Fridays, Saturdays and Sundays in the afternoon and is free to enter.

name: Radioweg
en: The Velibor Vasović Bridge (bridge 1906) is a structural work of art in Amsterdam-Oost. A concrete bridge, but then under number 426, provided the connection between the Watergraafsmeer district and the neighboring municipality of Diemen from 1983. These were then separated by the Ringweg-Oost and a ring ditch of Diemen. A joint span was then chosen.

name: Radioweg
en: The Velibor Vasovićbrug (bridge 1906) is a structure in Amsterdam-Oost. From 1983 a concrete bridge, then numbered 426, connected the Watergraafsmeer district with the neighbouring municipality of Diemen, which were separated by the eastern ring road and a Diemen ring ditch. A single shared span was chosen at the time.

name: Railway bridge over the Vliet
en: The Spoorbrug over de Vliet (also known as the High Bridge) is a railway bridge over the Vliet, located between the Dutch towns of Leidschendam and Voorburg.

name: Ransdorper Die
en: The Ransdorper Die is a creek, named, in Waterland in North Holland. The water lies north of the village of Ransdorp, which belongs to the municipality of Amsterdam, southwest of Holysloot and south of Broek in Waterland. It is also connected through the Nauw to the Holysloter Die north of Holysloot and further to the Uitdammer Die i

name: Ravensbrück memorial
en: Vrouwen van Ravensbrück 1940-1945 is a monument on the Museumplein in Amsterdam commemorating the Dutch victims of Ravensbrück, the Nazi concentration camp for women in Germany.

name: Raw Aron Schuster Synagoge
en: The Raw Aron Schuster Synagoge or the Obrechtsjoel (בית כנסת רב אהרן שוסטר) is the largest still functioning Ashkenazi synagogue (shoe) in Amsterdam. The synagogue, located at the corner of Jacob Obrechtplein and Heinzestraat in Amsterdam-Zuid, is part of the Jewish Community in Amsterdam, the NIHS. Most choepot (Jewish weddings) are held here.

name: RDM Campus
en: The RDM Campus is a campus on the site of the former Rotterdam Dry Dock Company (RDM), in the middle of Rotterdam's City Harbors. The area is being developed in phases into an attractive location for educational institutions and companies with an emphasis on sustainability. An important part of the RDM Campus is the former machine

name: Recreatieplas Strijkviertel
en: The Strijkviertelplas, official name Recreatieplas Strijkviertel, is a recreational lake in the city of Utrecht. The name Strijkviertel is that of a road nearby.

name: Rederijbrug
en: The Rederijbrug is a bascule bridge in the center of the Dutch city of Rotterdam. The bridge spans the Scheepmakershaven and forms the transition from the Rederijstraat to the Glashaven. This is the second bridge in this place.

name: Reesluis
en: The Reesluis (bridge 64) is a fixed bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Regentessebrug
en: The Regentessebrug is a fixed bridge in the Dutch city of Rotterdam. The bridge connects the Posthoornstraat with the Glashaven over the Wijnhaven. The Regentessebrug was built in 1898 to replace a wooden drawbridge and is one of the few pre-war structures that survived the bombing on May 14, 1940. The bridge is also popularly known as the

name: Rembrandt van Rijn statue
en: The Rembrandt monument is a 19th-century memorial to the painter Rembrandt van Rijn on the Rembrandtplein in Amsterdam. It is the oldest surviving statue in Amsterdam and was the first statue of a visual artist in the Netherlands.

name: Rhijnspoorplein
en: The Rhijnspoorplein is a square in Amsterdam-East and -Center. It is located between Weesperplein and Wibautstraat and is part of the Amsterdam city route s112, between the IJtunnel and the Gooiseweg. The square got its name in 1939. Previously, this was the Weesperpoort station from 1843 to 1939.

name: Rhijnspoorplein
en: The Rhijnspoorplein is a square in Amsterdam-East and -Center. It is located between Weesperplein and Wibautstraat and is part of the Amsterdam city route s112, between the IJtunnel and the Gooiseweg.

name: Riekerhavenbrug
en: Bridge 307 is a metal lifting bridge in southwest Amsterdam. The pedestrian and cyclist bridge is located in the Jaagpad and spans the halfway line between the Riekerhaven and Schinkel. Less than 10 meters west lies the Uiverbrug (bridge 2208), a "real" traffic bridge that has been connecting the Generaal Vetterstraat with the Valschermkade since 2003.

name: Riekerhavenbrug
en: Brug 307 is a metal drawbridge in the south-west of Amsterdam. The foot and cycle bridge lies in the Jaagpad and spans the dividing line between the Riekerhaven and the Schinkel. Less than 10 metres to the west lies the Uiverbrug (bridge 2208), a proper traffic bridge that has connected the Generaal Vetterstraat with the Valschermkade since 2003.

name: Rietlandpark
en: The Rietlandpark in Amsterdam-Oost was named in 2005 and is named after the Stads Rietlanden. This was until around 1880 an off-dikes uninhabited, partly swampy and reed-covered area. At the end of the 19th century, trade areas and a railway yard were built here as the center of the Eastern Harbor Area. This was also here until the

name: RiF010
en: RiF010 is an artificial water sports area with a water basin in and around the Steigersgracht, in the heart of Rotterdam. The area is located between the Hoogstraat and the Blaak; the water basin is located between the Grotemarkt and the Wezenbrug, just behind the Markthal.

name: Rijksakademie van beeldende kunsten
en: The Royal Academy of Fine Arts (also Royal Academy of Fine Arts) in Amsterdam was the highest art training institution in the Kingdom of the Netherlands from 1820 to 1870. Until 1830, it shared this role with the academy of Antwerp. The Academy was the successor to the City Drawing Academy. In 1870, the Academy was abolished and replaced by the

name: Rijnhaven
en: Rijnhaven is a former port of Rotterdam in transformation into a residential and working area within the Kop van Zuid district. The Rijnhaven is one of the oldest ports on the south bank of the Nieuwe Maas.

name: Rijnhavenbrug
en: The Rijnhavenbrug, locally known as the Hoerenloper, is a pedestrian and cyclist bridge over the Rotterdam Port in the Dutch city of Rotterdam. The bridge forms a connection between the Wilhelminapier at Hotel New York and Katendrecht.

name: Rijswijkseplein
en: The Rijswijkseplein is one of the busiest squares in The Hague. It is located between the Hoefkade and the Weteringkade, in the cross direction between the Zieken and the Rijswijkseweg, and close to Hollands Spoor station.

name: Rijswijkseweg
en: The Rijswijkseweg in The Hague, together with its extension, the Haagweg in Rijswijk, forms the connection between the Hoornbrug and the Rijswijkseplein. Traditionally, this was an important access road to The Hague from Utrecht and Rotterdam. This only changed with the opening of the Utrechtsebaan.

name: Ringvaart
en: The Ringvaart in Amsterdam-Oost is the name of the northern and eastern part of the ring canal around the Watergraafsmeer polder, which was reclaimed in 1629. The Ringvaart also forms the border of the Watergraafsmeer district (until 1921 a separate municipality and from 1987 to 1998 a district of Amsterdam).

name: Ringvaart van de Haarlemmermeerpolder
en: The Ringvaart van de Haarlemmermeerpolder is the more than 60 kilometer long ring road that runs around the Haarlemmermeerpolder.

name: Ringvaart van de Zuidplaspolder
en: The Ringvaart van de Zuidplaspolder is a canal in South Holland with a length of approximately 34 kilometers. The canal has a flexible water level of -2.30 m above sea level to -2.05 m above sea level. If mills and intakes are not used, the level is approximately at -2.15 above sea level everywhere.

name: Ringvaartbrug A5
en: The Ringvaartbrug A5, designated as Work of Art 511, is a work of art in the province of North Holland. The structure is located on the Rijksweg 5 / Westrandweg and crosses the Ringvaart of the Haarlemmermeer. The architectural firm Zwarts & Jansma Architecten was responsible for the design of this national road and all its works of art.

name: Ringvaartbrug A5
en: The Ringvaartbrug A5, designated Kunstwerk 511, is a structure in the province of North Holland. It lies in Rijksweg 5, the Westrandweg, and crosses the Ringvaart of the Haarlemmermeer. Zwarts & Jansma Architecten were responsible for the design of this motorway and all its structures.

name: Riouwstraat
en: The Riouwstraat is a street in the Archipelbuurt neighborhood in The Hague. It was laid out in 1879, at the same time as Billitonstraat and Madoerastraat. It was named after the Riouw Archipelago.

name: Robbenoordsehaven
en: The 1st Katendrechtsehaven, the 2nd Katendrechtsehaven, the Sint Janshaven and the Robbenoordsehaven were four small harbors on the southern bank of the Nieuwe Maas in Rotterdam, which all have lost their original function. The 1st Katendrechtsehaven has now been silenced; the 2nd partially. These four harbors show regarding their history of origin a

name: Robert Scottstraat
en: The Robert Scottstraat is a street in Amsterdam-West in the Robert Scott neighborhood named after him.

name: Rodenrijse Vaart
en: The Rodenrijse Vaart is a waterway in Berkel and Rodenrijs, in the Dutch province of South Holland. The canal (inner bay) is part of the water management of the Berkel polder. Parallel to the canal runs the Rodenrijseweg. The waterway runs from Oude Leede (Oude Bovendijk) in the west to Rodenrijs, and from there further northeast to he

name: Rolbrug bij Huis te Riviere
en: The Rolbrug bij Huis te Riviere is a rolling bridge over the Dutch waterway Schiedamse Schie. It connects the Overschieseweg in the Rotterdam municipality of Overschie with the Polderweg in Schiedam-Kethel.

name: Rooseveltlaan
en: The Rooseveltlaan is a street in the Rivierenbuurt in Amsterdam-Zuid. The avenue is characterized by the poplars standing on either side of the carriageway. Unlike originally the Amstellaan and the Noorder Amstellaan, there is no wide central lawn.

name: Rosa Overbeekbrug
en: The Rosa Overbeekbrug (bridge no. 121) is a bridge over the Bloemgracht in the Jordaan in Amsterdam, connecting the Eerste Bloemdwarsstraat with the Tweede Leliedwarsstraat. A bridge has been here for centuries: both Balthasar Florisz. van Berckenrode and Joan Blaeu drew one on their maps of 1625 and 1649.

name: Rosarium
en: The Rosarium Oudwijk in the Dutch city of Utrecht is a rose garden in the Wilhelminapark neighborhood and surroundings on the east side of the city. The garden is part of a green structure in a north-south direction that connects Wilhelminapark with the Hogelandsepark, as well as Oorsprongpark.

name: Rosestraat
en: The Rosestraat and the 2nd Rosestraat are a street approximately 1.5 kilometers and 400 meters long in the Rotterdam municipality of Feijenoord.

name: Rosette Vilbach-Blom
en: The List of Stolpersteine in Hillegersberg-Schiebroek provides an overview of the commemorative stones placed in the city district of Hillegersberg-Schiebroek in the Dutch municipality of Rotterdam as part of the Stolpersteine project of the German sculptor-artist Gunter Demnig. Stolpersteine are dedicated to victims of the National Socialism

name: Rotterdammerbrug
en: The Rotterdammerbrug (bridge 150) is a fixed bridge on the boundary of Amsterdam-Centrum and Amsterdam Oud-West. It spans the Singelgracht between the Marnixstraat and the Nassaukade. On the east side it meets the Eerste Marnixplantsoen, laid out on the former Bolwerk Haarlem, one of Amsterdam's 17th-century bastions.

name: Rotterdammerbrug
en: The Rotterdammerbrug (bridge 150) is a fixed bridge on the border of Amsterdam-Centrum and Amsterdam Oud-West. The bridge spans the Singelgracht between Marnixstraat and Nassaukade. On the east side, the bridge opens into Eerste Marnixplantsoen, built on the former Bolwerk Haarlem, one of the 17th-century Amsterdam bastions. The first bridge was a bo

name: Rotterdams Openbaar Vervoer Museum
en: The RoMeO foundation is an organization that deals with the operation of old trams, subways and buses in Rotterdam and stands for "Rotterdams Openbaar Vervoer museum and Operation of Oldtimers". RoMeO was founded in 1997 and brings together the activities of various organizations that had previously been involved in the history of the Rotterdamse

name: Rotterdamsche Schie
en: The Rotterdam Schie is a largely dammed canal between Overschie and Rotterdam.

name: Rotterdamsebaan
en: The Rotterdamsebaan, during the planning phase called Trekvliettracé, has been a road in The Hague since February 2021, connecting the A4 and A13 with the Centrumring. Most of the road consists of the Victory Boogie Woogietunnel, which runs under the Voorburg-West district, among other things.

name: Royal Tropical Institute
en: The KIT building is a complex of buildings in Amsterdam-Oost, built from 1915 to 1926 for the accommodation of the Colonial Institute and museum. The architect Johannes van Nieukerken designed the building. After his death in 1913, it was then completed by his sons Johan and Marie Adrianus van Nieukerken. It was financed by contributions from among others

name: Rozenoordmetrobrug
en: The Rozenoord Bridge (bridge no. 174P (A10)) consists of two traffic bridges over the Amstel River in Amsterdam. The bridges connect Amsterdam-Zuid with Overamstel. Between the two traffic bridges are three railway bridges; one for the Amsterdam metro and two for the train traffic of the Dutch Railways on the Weesp - Leiden railway line. All b

name: Rozenoordspoorbrug
en: The Rozenoordbrug (bridge no. 174P, A10) consists of two traffic bridges over the river Amstel in Amsterdam, connecting Amsterdam-Zuid with Overamstel. Between the two road bridges lie three railway bridges: one for the Amsterdam metro and two for Nederlandse Spoorwegen trains on the Weesp-Leiden line.

name: Rozenoordspoorbrug
en: The Rozenoord Bridge (bridge no. 174P (A10)) consists of two traffic bridges over the Amstel River in Amsterdam. The bridges connect Amsterdam-Zuid with Overamstel. Between the two traffic bridges are three railway bridges; one for the Amsterdam metro and two for the train traffic of the Dutch Railways on the Weesp - Leiden railway line. All b

name: Rubenslaan
en: The Rubenslaan is a street in the Dutch city of Utrecht, which runs from Venuslaan to Adriaen van Ostadelaan and Stadionlaan where it merges into it.

name: Rubenslaan
en: Rubenslaan can refer to: Rubenslaan (Utrecht), street in Utrecht Rubenslaan and surroundings (Utrecht), a neighborhood in the Oost district of Utrecht

name: Rudolf Manheim
en: The List of Stolpersteine in Hillegersberg-Schiebroek provides an overview of the commemorative stones placed in the city district of Hillegersberg-Schiebroek in the Dutch municipality of Rotterdam as part of the Stolpersteine project of the German sculptor-artist Gunter Demnig. Stolpersteine are dedicated to victims of the National Socialism

name: Ruud Krolbrug
en: The Ruud Krolbrug (bridge 2232) is a structure in Amsterdam-Oost. It is one of the foot and cycle bridges in the Park de Meer neighbourhood in Watergraafsmeer, built here between 1998 and 2002 and entirely surrounded by a ring ditch. It connects the Wembleylaan, inside the neighbourhood, with the Radioweg outside it.

name: Ruud Krolbrug
en: The Ruud Krolbrug (bridge 2232) is a structural work of art in Amsterdam-Oost. The bridge is one of the pedestrian and bicycle bridges in the area of Park de Meer, Watergraafsmeer that rose from the ground here between 1998 and 2002. That area is completely surrounded by a water channel/ring ditch.

name: Ryckerbrug
en: The Rijckerbrug or Ryckerbrug (bridge no. 167) is a fixed slab bridge between Amsterdam-Centrum and Amsterdam-West crossing the Singelgracht. It connects the Rozengracht, called the Verlengde Rozengracht while it was being built, with the De Clercqstraat, and has its western abutment in the Nassaukade.

name: Salomon Vilbach
en: The List of Stolpersteine in Hillegersberg-Schiebroek provides an overview of the commemorative stones placed in the city district of Hillegersberg-Schiebroek in the Dutch municipality of Rotterdam as part of the Stolpersteine project of the German sculptor-artist Gunter Demnig. Stolpersteine are dedicated to victims of the National Socialism

name: Samen Spelen Samen Leven
en: The Kindermonument Markt voor Joden, also called Samen spelen, samen leven, is an artistic work in Amsterdam-Zuid. It is a group of three sculptures by Truus Menger-Oversteegen, placed since 1986 at the entrance to the playground on the Gaaspstraat, between the even-numbered buildings on the Vechtstraat and the odd-numbered ones on the Gaaspstraat.

name: Sara de Vries
en: The list of Stolpersteine in Utrecht (municipality) gives an overview of the commemorative stones that have been placed in the municipality of Utrecht in the Dutch province of Utrecht as part of the Stolpersteine project of the German sculptor-artist Gunter Demnig. Stolpersteine are dedicated to victims of Nazism, all those who were murdered by it.

name: Sara Elisabeth van Gelderen
en: The list of Stolpersteine in Utrecht (municipality) gives an overview of the commemorative stones that have been placed in the municipality of Utrecht in the Dutch province of Utrecht as part of the Stolpersteine project of the German sculptor-artist Gunter Demnig. Stolpersteine are dedicated to victims of Nazism, all those who were murdered by it.

name: Sarphatimonument
en: The Sarphatimonument honours the 19th-century Jewish Amsterdam physician and benefactor Samuel Sarphati and stands in the Sarphatipark in the De Pijp district. It was built in 1886 on a small mound made for it in the park. It is a round, temple-like stone structure 12 metres high, designed by Jacobus Roeland de Kruijff.

name: Sarphatimonument
en: The Sarphatimonument is a monument in honor of the 19th-century Jewish Amsterdam physician and benefactor Samuel Sarphati, in Sarphatipark in the Amsterdam district of de Pijp. The monument was built in 1886 on a small hill specially built for this purpose in the park.

name: Sartreweg
en: The Sartreweg is a road in the east of the city of Utrecht.

name: Scharrebiersluis
en: The Scharrebiersluis (bridge 278) is a lift bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum. The bridge is named after scharrebier, a cheap beer of moderate quality that was bought on site here by waiting captains. The bridge forms the connection between Rapenburgplein and Foeliedwarsstraat on Rapenburg on the west side and Kadijksplein and the Laagte Kadijk on

name: Scharrebiersluis
en: The Scharrebiersluis is a pick-up bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum. The bridge is named after scharrebier, a cheap beer of moderate quality that was bought on site here by waiting ship captains.

name: Scheepmakershaven
en: The Scheepmakershaven is a port in Rotterdam.

name: Schellingwouderbreek
en: The Schellingwouderbreek is a lake in Amsterdam-North. The breakwater is a provincial monument.

name: Schellingwouderbrug
en: The Schellingwouderbrug (bridge no. 55P) is a traffic bridge over the Buiten IJ in Amsterdam, connecting Zeeburgereiland in Amsterdam-Oost with Amsterdam-Noord. In line with it lies the Amsterdamsebrug over the Amsterdam-Rijnkanaal, between Zeeburgereiland and the Zeeburgerdijk near the Flevopark in the Indische Buurt.

name: Schellingwouderbrug
en: The Schellingwouderbrug (bridge no. 55P) is a traffic bridge over the Buiten IJ in Amsterdam. The bridge connects the Zeeburgereiland (Amsterdam-East) and Amsterdam-North with each other.

name: Schenkkade
en: The Schenkkade in the Hague district of Bezuidenhout runs parallel to the Schenkwetering, which was mentioned as early as the 14th century. The water was dug shortly after the construction of the Spui and was mainly used to transport peat barges with peat from the then bare Bezuidenhout to the center of The Hague.

name: Scheurhaven
en: The Scheurhaven is a port in Rotterdam's Europoort on the Caland Canal. It is located at the head of the North Sea Road on the Landtong of Rozenburg between the Caland Canal and the Nieuwe Waterweg. The port is mainly used by tugboats, but also by oil-containment vessels from HEBO.

name: Scheveningsebrug
en: Scheveningsebrug is the name of a bridge in the northwest of the historic city center of The Hague. This bridge is the connection of the Noordeinde over the Noord Singelsgracht to the Zeestraat. In the past, the bridge was also often called the Noord-Valbrug and the Noordeinde Brug.

name: Scheveningseweg
en: The Scheveningseweg is a long, straight street between the old center of The Hague and Scheveningen, which was built in 1665 according to a design by Constantijn Huygens.

name: Schie-Schiekanaal
en: The Schie-Schiekanaal is a waterway in Rotterdam that forms the connection between the Delfshavense Schie and the Rotterdamse Schie.

name: Schiedamsedijk
en: The Schiedamsedijk is a road in the center of Rotterdam, which connects the Erasmus Bridge with the Coolsingel and the (West-)Blaak.

name: Schiedamseweg
en: The Schiedamseweg is a well-known shopping street in the Rotterdam municipality of Delfshaven. The Schiedamseweg runs between the Aelbrechtskolk in historic Delfshaven and the Marconiplein. From the Marconiplein, the Schiedamseweg runs as part of Schielands Hoge Zeedijk through to the municipal border of Schiedam. This section is commonly known as Rotterd

name: Schiehaven
en: The Schiehaven is a pre-war harbor in the Lloyd district in Rotterdam-Delfshaven. The Schiehaven was dug between 1904 and 1909 and designed for the transhipment of bulk goods. On the east side of the Schiehaven was the Schiecentrale. The supply of coal for the Schiehavencentrale was by ship. The power plant operated until 1990

name: Schieweg
en: Schieweg (Schieoevers) is a district in Delft, in the Dutch province of South Holland. The district borders the Delft Schie. There are few houses, it is mainly an industrial area. Most companies are located along the Schieweg, hence the name of the district. Among others, the Makro is located in this district.

name: Schinkel
en: The Schinkel is a small canalized river in Amsterdam, in the Dutch province of North Holland. The river runs from the (former) Overtoomse Sluis to the Nieuwe Meer.

name: Schollenbrug
en: The Schollenbrug (bridge 340) is a fixed bridge in Amsterdam-Oost. The traffic bridge lies in the Weesperzijde and spans the Ringvaart of the Watergraafsmeer at the Amstel.

name: Seinehaven
en: The Seinehaven is a port in the east of the Europoort area in Rotterdam on the Hartel Canal. The port was built in 1969. Districenter Botlek, the Botlek factory of Lyondell Chemical Company and the Holland Terminals of PSA-HNN are located here, among others.

name: Seranggracht
en: The Serangracht is a canal with associated embankments in Amsterdam-Oost, classified under the Indian Quarter.

name: Servaasbrug
en: The Servaasbrug is a bridge in the Dutch city of Utrecht. The fixed bridge is made of stone and is located in the southeast corner of the Museum Quarter in the Utrecht city center. There it forms the southernmost bridge over the Nieuwegracht that flows out under the bridge into the Stadsbuitengracht.

name: Seychellen
en: The Seychellen, officially the Republic of the Seychellen, are a country and archipelago in Africa north of Madagascar in the Indian Ocean, about 1600 km east of the African continent. The Seychellen consist of more than 115 islands. Less than a third of them are inhabited. Of the 95,981 (2020) inhabitants, about 90% live on the main island Mahé, da

name: Shadow quay
en: De Schaduwkade is a monument to two hundred Jewish residents of the Nieuwe Keizersgracht in Amsterdam who were murdered in the Second World War. It consists of two hundred metal plates bearing the residents' names, grouped around the number of the house where they lived on the other side of the water.

name: Siegerpark
en: The Siegerpark is a small city park on the Sloterweg in the Riekerpolder in Amsterdam-Nieuw-West. The name is not recorded in the Basic Registration of Addresses and Buildings.

name: Simon Carmiggelt
en: The Bust of Simon Carmiggelt is a work of art in Amsterdam-Centrum. In November 1987, writer Simon Carmiggelt, a well-known Amsterdam personality, died. Soon after, the idea came up to have a statue erected in the city as a tribute. Friends, acquaintances of the writer and the public under the leadership of actor Ton van Duinhoven raised money. Van Du

name: Singel
en: Muntsluis can refer to: Muntsluis (Amsterdam), a bridge in Amsterdam (with the Muntplein) Muntsluis (Utrecht), a lock complex in the Merwedekanaal (with the Muntbrug)

name: Singelgrachtbrug
en: The Houtmanspoorbrug, colloquially known as the Singelgrachtbrug, is a system of lift bridges in Amsterdam-Centrum, near the Spaarndammerbuurt district. The bridge spans the Westerkanaal with its western quay, the Houtmankade. Until November 2017, the bridge was known as S4 (rail bridge 4) or Singelgrachtbrug. The Westerkanaal is indeed part of the Singelgra

name: Singelgrachtbrug
en: The Houtmanspoorbrug, popularly called the Singelgrachtbrug, is a set of drawbridges in Amsterdam-Centrum on the edge of the Spaarndammerbuurt. It spans the Westerkanaal and its western quay, the Houtmankade. Until November 2017 it was known as S4 or the Singelgrachtbrug, as the Westerkanaal lies in line with the Singelgracht.

name: Singelkerk
en: The Singelkerk is a church of the Mennonite congregation in Amsterdam, lying between the Singel and the Herengracht. It is a clandestine church, one that is not recognisable as a church from the outside.

name: Sint Agneskerk
en: The Sint-Agneskerk is a Roman Catholic church on Beeklaan in The Hague. The church building and the congregation are part of the parish of Maria Sterre der Zee. The church was built in 1902 and 1903 under the direction of the architectural firm of Albert Margry and Jozef Snickers.

name: Sint Antoniesluis
en: Sint Antoniesluis or Sint Anthoniesluis can refer to: old name for the Sint Antoniessluishoogwaterkering, a lock in Amsterdam-Centrum Sint Antoniesluis (street), a street on the quay of the pool of the aforementioned lock Sint Anthoniesluis (bridge), a traffic bridge over the aforementioned lock

name: Sint Jobshaven
en: The Sint Jobshaven is a pre-war port in the Rotterdam municipality of Delfshaven. The Sint Jobshaven was dug between 1906 and 1908 and built for the transhipment of bulk goods. The port is named after the demolished Sint Jobskapel during the construction of the port in the former village of Schoonderloo.

name: Sint Martinusbrug
en: The Sint Martinusbrug or simply Martinusbrug is a fixed bridge in the center of the Dutch city of Utrecht. It spans the Stadsbuitengracht (Catharijnesingel) It is a pedestrian tunnel bridge made of steel with a concrete bridge deck. It was built according to the design of the Dutch architect Wiek Röling. In preparation for the final

name: Sint Nicolaasbrug
en: The Sint Nicolaasbrug (bridge 306) is a fixed bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum. The bridge spans the Open Havenfront and extends along the Damrak. The bridge connects the Prins Hendrikkade with the Stationsplein in front of Amsterdam Central Station. This led to its unofficial name Stationsbrug. Since it was the middle of three bridges in front of the s

name: Sint Nicolaasbrug
en: The Sint Nicolaasbrug (bridge 306) is a fixed bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum. It spans the Open Havenfront in line with the Damrak, connecting the Prins Hendrikkade with the Stationsplein in front of Amsterdam Centraal station. That gave it the unofficial name Stationsbrug, as it was the middle of the three bridges to the station.

name: Sint Olofskapel
en: The Sint-Olofkapel, or Oudezijds Kapel, is a building in the Dutch city of Amsterdam. The former church building is located in the city center of Amsterdam, between the Zeedijk and the Nieuwebrugsteeg, near the Damrak. The first Sint Olofskapel was built between 1440 and 1450 against a large city gate, the Sint Olofspoort.

name: Sint Olofskapel
en: The Sint-Olofskapel, or Oudezijds Kapel, is a building in Amsterdam. The former church stands in the inner city between the Zeedijk and the Nieuwebrugsteeg, near the Damrak. The first Sint-Olofskapel was built between 1440 and 1450 against a large city gate, the Sint Olofspoort, which was demolished in 1618.

name: Sint Paschalis Baylon
en: The Sint-Paschalis Baylon Church on the Wassenaarseweg in The Hague was built between 1919 and 1921. The church is named after the Spanish saint Paschalis Baylon. The nearby school is also named after the church. The church is a good example of the traditionalist architectural style of A.J. Kropholler, who had not built such a large church before.

name: Sint-Agneskerk
en: The Sint-Agneskerk in Amsterdam is a Catholic parish church, located at the corner of Amstelveenseweg 163 and Cornelis Krusemanstraat, on the Haarlemmermeercircuit and on the edge of the Willemspark neighborhood.

name: Sint-Agneskerk
en: The Sint-Agneskerk in Amsterdam is a Catholic parish church on the corner of Amstelveenseweg 163 and the Cornelis Krusemanstraat, at the Haarlemmermeercircuit on the edge of the Willemsparkbuurt. Dedicated to the martyr St Agnes, it was built between 1919 and 1932 to a design by the architect Jan Stuyt and listed as a national monument in 1996.

name: Sint-Aloysiuskerk
en: The Sint-Aloysiuskerk is a Roman Catholic church building in the Dutch city of Utrecht, in the subdistrict/neighborhood Abstede in the Oost district. The church is dedicated to the saint Aloysius.

name: Sint-Augustinuskerk
en: The Sint-Augustinuskerk is a Roman Catholic church in the Dutch city of Utrecht, on the northern part of the Oudegracht (no. 69), dedicated to Augustine of Hippo.

name: Sint-Bavo
en: The Sint-Bavokerk is a Roman Catholic parish church in the Rotterdam district of Pendrecht. The church is the church building of the 'O.L.V. van Lourdes parish' which is part of the 'Parish Federation Maria Magdalena'. As part of the 'Designation Program Reconstruction 1940-1945', the church building was designated as a national monument in 2019.

name: Sint-Gertrudiskerk
en: The Sint-Gertrudiskerk is a former Roman Catholic church building in the village of Ruigoord in the municipality of Amsterdam in the Dutch province of North Holland. The church was designed by C.P.W. Dessing and was dedicated to the Holy Gertrude of Nijvel. In the church there is a statue of Gertrudis with a staff with mice.

name: Sint-Gertrudiskerk
en: The Sint-Gertrudiskerk is a former Roman Catholic church in the village of Ruigoord in the municipality of Amsterdam, North Holland. It was designed by C.P.W. Dessing and dedicated to St Gertrude of Nivelles. Inside stands a statue of Gertrude with a staff and mice. The church was taken out of use in 1973.

name: Sint-Jacobsbrug
en: The Sint-Jacobsbrug is a fixed bridge in the center of the Dutch city of Rotterdam. The bridge spans the Stokviswater and is part of the Binnenrotte. The bridge was built around 1960 as a temporary bridge on the site of the Stokkenbrug in the Schiedamsedijk over the Zalmhaven, which had been demolished due to the construction of the subway.

name: Sint-Jacobsstraat
en: The Monicabrug is a fixed bridge in the Dutch city of Utrecht. The bridge is located in the northern part of the center. It spans the Stadsbuitengracht (Weerdsingel) and forms a direct connection between the Sint Jacobsstraat and the Oudenoord. The bridge was built according to the design of the Dutch architect Wiek Röling and was opened in 2001.

name: Sint-Jacobus de Meerderekerk
en: The Sint-Jacobus de Meerderekerk (also: Jacobuskerk) is a Roman Catholic church on Parkstraat in the center of The Hague. The church building and the congregation are part of the parish Maria Sterre der Zee.

name: Sint-Lambertuskerk
en: The Sint-Lambertuskerk is a Roman Catholic church in Rotterdam-Kralingen. The Lambertus Church is located at the corner of the Beneden Oostzeedijk and the Hoflaan. It was designed in neo-Gothic style by Evert Margry, a pupil of P.J.H. Cuypers, and built in the period 1875-1878.

name: Sint-Laurenshaven
en: The Sint Laurenshaven is a port in the Botlek area in Rotterdam. The main companies at the Sint Laurenshaven are Vopak with a tank storage company and EBS with a specialized transhipment company for dry mineral bulk products. In addition to storage outdoors, storage also takes place in tanks with a conical roof for those products that are humid

name: Sint-Liduina
en: The Sint-Liduinakerk is a Catholic church on Burgemeester Le Fèvre de Montignylaan in Hillegersberg (Rotterdam municipality). The church is named after Liduina van Schiedam. Due to the growth of the village, the Sint-Hildegard church was no longer sufficient to serve the Catholic community.

name: Sint-Pauluskerk
en: The Sint-Pauluskerk is a church building at Larikslaan 182 in Schiebroek, a part of Rotterdam.

name: Sint-Petrus-en-Pauluskerk
en: The Sint-Petrus-en-Pauluskerk is an Old Catholic church on the Ruysdaelstraat in the Duivelseiland district of Amsterdam. The church, presbytery and teaching room form a whole and were designed by Johan W.F. Hartkamp jr., a pupil of Hendrik Petrus Berlage. The complex was completed in 1914 as a continuation of the clandestine church De Ooievaar.

name: Sint-Petrus-en-Pauluskerk
en: The Sint-Petrus-en-Pauluskerk is a Dutch Old Catholic church building on Ruysdaelstraat in the Duivelseiland district of Amsterdam. The church, parsonage and teaching room form a whole and were designed by Johan W.F. Hartkamp jr., a pupil of Hendrik Petrus Berlage. The church complex was completed in 1914 as a precursor to the secret church 'De Ooievaar'

name: Sint-Rafaëlkerk
en: The Sint-Rafaëlkerk is a church building of the Roman Catholic Church in the Overvecht district in the Dutch city of Utrecht. The church is located at the corner of Lichtenberchdreef with the Neckardreef and on the edge of the Park de Watertoren. The church is dedicated to the archangel Raphael and is used by the Ludgerus parish.

name: Sinti- en Roma monument
en: The Roma and Sinti monument in the Haagse Vondelstraat opposite the Bilderdijkstraat is a cube-shaped object with a bronze commemorative plaque.

name: Sisyfusgemaal
en: The Sisyfusgemaal is both a structural and artistic work of art (applied art) in Amsterdam Nieuw-West.

name: Sixhaven
en: Sixhaven can refer to: Sixhaven (harbor), a marina on the IJ in Amsterdam-North Sixhaven (metro station), a possible future metro station in Amsterdam-North

name: Slinge
en: The Slinge is the central axis of the Rotterdam neighborhoods of Zuidwijk and Pendrecht. The Slinge is almost 3.5 kilometers long and runs from the Groene Kruisweg in the west to the Dordtsestraatweg in the east. The house numbering starts at 3 at the Dordtsestraatweg and goes up to 901 at the Groene Kruisweg.

name: Sloterbrug
en: The Sloterbrug (bridge 9P) is a drawbridge within the municipality of Haarlemmermeer. The bridge belongs to Haarlemmermeer but is known in Amsterdam as bridge 9P, the P meaning not maintained by Amsterdam. Officially the bridge has no name.

name: Sloterdijkerbrug
en: The Sloterdijkerbrug (bridge 321) is a double wooden drawbridge in Amsterdam-Centrum. It spans the Prinseneilandsgracht. It not only forms the main route between Sloterdijkstraat on the mainland and Galgenstraat on Prinseneiland, but also between both quays of that canal Nieuwe Teertuinen and Prinseneiland, the street. Around the bridge is a

name: Sloterdijkerbrug
en: The Sloterdijkerbrug (bridge 321) is a double wooden drawbridge in Amsterdam-Centrum. It spans the Prinseneilandsgracht, forming both the through route between the Sloterdijkstraat on the mainland and the Galgenstraat on Prinseneiland, and the link between that canal's two quays, the Nieuwe Teertuinen and Prinseneiland.

name: Sloterkerk
en: The Sloterkerk is a Protestant church in Sloten, North Holland.

name: Slotermeerlaan
en: The Slotermeerlaan is a street in Amsterdam Nieuw-West. The street runs from west to south and begins at the circuit at Burgemeester De Vlugtlaan/Antony Moddermanstraat. Then the street turns right at an angle and crosses De Vlugtlaan again. Then the street runs along Plein '40-'45, crosses Henriette Roland Holststraat/Lodewijk

name: Sloterplas
en: The Sloterplas is located in the center of the Western Garden Cities in Amsterdam Nieuw-West. The pond was dug between 1948 and 1956 and has a maximum depth of 37 meters.

name: Slufter
en: The Slufter is a large-scale storage facility for contaminated sludge in the southwestern part of the Rotterdam Maasvlakte on the North Sea coast near Voorne. Construction took place in 1986 and 1987. The depot is initially intended for the storage of contaminated dredged material, resulting from regular maintenance dredging work in the waterways to and from

name: Sluis Haarlemmervaart
en: The Schutsluis Haarlemmervaart stands in the Haarlemmervaart in Amsterdam-West at Van Slingelandtstraat. The lock, with a chamber length of 36.44 metres and a passage width of 6 metres, was built after the Haarlemmervaart lost its tow-canal role in the 19th century and a direct connection was made near Nassauplein.

name: Smal Weesp
en: Smal Weesp is a channeled stream between the Vecht River and the Amsterdam-Rhine Canal. It flows across Weesp. In Driemond, the Smal Weesp joined the Gein and Gaasp streams. That explains the naming of that place.

name: Smeebrug
en: The Smeebrug is a nationally protected arched bridge in the city center of Utrecht. The bridge spans the Oudegracht. The name of the bridge is derived from the guild of blacksmiths, who lived in this area.

name: Smidswater
en: The Hague canal belt is the (partly 16th and especially early) 17th-century Singelsgracht that is still intact. A belt is ring-shaped, or circular, the Singelsgracht in The Hague has a different (angular) shape. That is not unique. Old Rotterdam had a triangular shape. A canal belt should not be confused with a system of interconnected waterways.

name: Snodenhoekpark
en: The Snodenhoekpark is a small park and a street in the Gaasperdam district in Amsterdam-Zuidoost. The park is located south of the Schoonhovendreef and north of De Hoge Dijk. The Steengroevenpad runs through the park. The park was built in the mid-1980s, at the same time as the Reigersbos district, part of Gaasperdam. The park is named after d

name: Sociëteit De Vereeniging
en: Sociëteit De Vereeniging in The Hague is a gentlemen's society founded on April 30, 1851. The first members were 79 gentlemen, who temporarily met in a rented building at Kazernestraat 198 in The Hague, where seven years later the Hotel Des Indes would be built. There were already several gentlemen's clubs in The Hague in 1851: the Grande Société dates back

name: Socratesbrug
en: The Socratesbrug is a bascule bridge over the Merwedekanaal in the city of Utrecht. The bridge was opened in 1964 and forms a connection between the Transwijk and Rivierenwijk districts, respectively the Beneluxlaan and the Socrateslaan, in the south of the city.

name: Soestwetering
en: The Soestwetering is a main watercourse in Salland in the Dutch province of Overijssel. It springs from the foot of the Holterberg. The ditch runs from the Holtense hamlet of Dijkerhoek through a large part of Salland towards Zwolle. Here it joins the Nieuwe Wetering and the Almelose Canal. After crossing the Stadsgracht, this canal runs v

name: Solebayplein
en: Solebayplein is an unofficial name for a square in the Landlust district in Amsterdam-West.

name: Solitudobrug
en: The Solitudobrug (bridge 2190) is a structure in Amsterdam-Oost.

name: Solitudolaanspoorbrug
en: The Solitudolaanspoorbrug lies in Amsterdam-Oost, along with the Solitudolaan and the Solitudopad. The lane and path were named in 2015, when new housing was built in the area and the roads were rearranged; the railway bridge was named after the lane in February 2018. The viaduct was built in two stages.

name: Solitudolaanspoorbrug
en: The Solitudolaanspoorbrug, whose coordinates are Solitudolaan and Solitudopad in Amsterdam-Oost. The Solitudolaan and -pad received their names in 2015, when new residential buildings were built in this area and road redevelopment took place. The railway bridge was named after the avenue in February 2018.

name: Sonneveld House
en: House Sonneveld in the South Holland city of Rotterdam was built between 1932 and 1933 by architect Leendert van der Vlugt of Bureau Brinkman & van der Vlugt on behalf of A.H. Sonneveld, then member of the board of directors of the Rotterdam company Erven De Weduwe J. van Nelle.

name: Sophialaan
en: Sophialaan can refer to: Sophialaan (Amsterdam) Sophialaan (Baarn) Sophialaan 3 (Baarn) Sophialaan 14 (Baarn) Sophialaan 19-21 (Baarn) Sophialaan 23-25 (Baarn) Sophialaan 27-29 (Baarn) Sophialaan Sophialaan (Leeuwarden) Sophialaan (Nijmegen)

name: Spaansebrug
